item.title: A favorite bass performance from La Grunowa - Parterre Box
item.description: Tancredi Pasero is so noble in mien and rich-voiced here, a perfect complement to Caniglia's earthy Leonora who honestly charts the movement from despair to fervent, transcendent faith in this duet.

item.title: The company of wolves - Parterre Box
item.description: Matthias Pintscher’s Nuit sans aube at the Opéra Comique conjures up plenty of atmosphere — but not much else.

item.title: The art of the possible - Parterre Box
item.description: Ahead of his first season as the Music &amp;amp; Artistic Director of the New York Philharmonic, how much longer can -- and should -- Gustavo Dudamel stay quiet about the situation in his native Venezuela?

item.title: A favorite bass performance from Eli Jacobson - Parterre Box
item.description: This bass aria "Sous les pieds d'une femme" from Gounod's La Reine du Saba used to be a concert favorite

item.title: Rags to riches - Parterre Box
item.description: In its first production since departing the Kennedy Center, the Washington National Opera presents a new adaptation of "King of Ragtime" Scott Joplin’s opera Treemonisha.

item.title: Life imitates art - Parterre Box
item.description: With Gustavo Dudamel in the spotlight at Parterre Box this week, Grand Tier Grab Bag foreshadows one of the New York Philharmonic's upcoming operatic engagements.

item.title: A favorite bass performance from William Guanbo Su - Parterre Box
item.description: This performance was introduced to me by Norman Treigle’s granddaughter —very fine mezzo-soprano Emily Treigle; while I was preparing the role of Olin Blitch, and it completely changed my understanding of the character.

item.title: Gild the Lily - Parterre Box
item.description: Lisette Oropesa, Piotr Buszewski, and Luca Salsi feature in a rote revival of Michael Mayer's cloying production of La traviata.

item.title: Road shows - Parterre Box
item.description: Brendan Latimer hitches a ride with members of the "site-responsive opera" movement who are taking their shows out of the opera house -- and out of the box.

item.title: A favorite bass performance from TildyDiva - Parterre Box
item.description: The greatest bass performance I ever experienced was actually four – four performances in four roles.

item.title: Follow the signs - Parterre Box
item.description: Opera directors could learn a thing or two from Deaf Broadway's vivacious performance of Jeanine Tesori's Violet.

item.title: A favorite bass performance from Christopher Corwin - Parterre Box
item.description: As we reach the end of “Bass Month” I’d like to call attention to the superb American Gregory Reinhart who particularly shone in music by Jean-Philippe Rameau.

item.title: A favorite performance from Margarete Cum Klose - Parterre Box
item.description: Pure class. Kurt Moll really knew his own voice inside out.

item.title: Which witch? - Parterre Box
item.description: Washington National Opera offered a searing production of Robert Ward’s opera The Crucible, directed by WNO Artistic Director Francesca Zambello, as the second installment in the company’s next chapter.

item.title: Suffering a sea-change - Parterre Box
item.description: Calixto Bieito's production of Idomeneo at La Monnaie is anchored by a committed cast, but gets swept up in pseudo-psychoanalytic imagery — and foot fetishism.
